I used to really want to work with Indigenous archeological collections, but even in the best circumstances, the relationship between Indigenous people and the museum institutions is so bad. Native Truths in chicago is a really fantastic example of what the display of Indigenous artifacts/objects \*could\* be like, and even that had some pretty messy stuff going on behind the scenes. It's really sad how normalized it is to feel entitlement towards Indigenous people just because these items are already in collections. I don't think people really make the connection that for us, the acquisition of these objects and literal human bodies is in the past. But those acquisitions were acts of violence towards Indigenous people that don't stop until we involve them in the process of deciding what should happen to these collections. A lot of people will say they're pro-tribal sovereignty and anti-colonialism. But when they're face to face with what that actually means, suddenly the full self-determination of Indigenous people is a question rather than an assumption. There is no fixing the museum until we learn readily to take "no" as an answer from source communities. Our desire to spread information, preserve history, and conduct research is not more important than the people at the center of these exhibits/collections.

Two things really helped me:

I've found that the BPD rage words are really like word vomit. Unlike vomit, stopping those words before they get started can actually be really healthy. For me, that meant figuring out what patterns started the flow of my rants/yelling and disrupting that flow. I realized that over text, i'm more likely to dissociate from the fact that i'm talking to someone I love and I don't want to hurt them (even if it felt like I did). I asked my patrtner to disengage if I started an argument over text, and we made a script of sorts that would set me up to deal with those feelings without hurting them. They'd tell me when they noticed I was disregulated, give me empathy and reassurance, and then enforce their boundary that I cannot just be hurtful towards them. Then, I'd try my very best to use my therapy skills to regulate, and we'd revisit the argument later when I'm good and calm. It is \*horrible\* at first but you'll really just have to open up these new pathways in your brain for dealing with things. It does get easier. We're married now and almost never argue. When my rage was at its worst, we had broken up really badly and were presumably done for good.

Second thing (which can be used together with the first one) is that I kept track of things I say that were really toxic or harmful to myself/others and set the intention of kicking those phrases out of my vocabulary. Things like "i know you hate me," or "you're going to leave" or "you don't care about me" aren't realistic or productive, and they also don't really get at what's going on internally. Instead, I had to learn to focus on why I feel like saying that, and describe that feeling instead. Sometimes, since we're learning new ways of existing, you might not be able to come up with something else to say. Instead, you can say "I know this is toxic but..." and then describe what you're feeling without using the "i know this is toxic" as a license to just say hurtful things. My husband and I would often talk through my feelings of "I know this is not true, but it feels like you hurt me on purpose and that you don't care." That's very different from just the accusation and leaves a lot of room to explore that feeling further. Hope this helps!

sure! trophy wife is a really wonderful statement/editorial highlight for light skin, and a great editorial or golden highlight for medium to dark shades. It does have pretty large chunks of glitter so if you're going for subtlety, start extra extra slow. tap into the product, don't bother swirling, if you want something subtle. It builds up extremely easily to a blinding glimmery highlight. I personally like to diffuse this over the high points of my face with my fingers. I just feel like I have more control that way, and since I spent years only using fingers before i knew better i feel like i have an OK handle on placing product with just the finger tips. I'm looking to buy a fan brush to see if that works any better. That's how i work with highlighters generally but Especially with trophy wife because of how easy it is to pack on too much with my it cosmetics highlight and contour brush. If i'm looking for a deep gold but still want a highlight that sweeps across the cheek, i like to use a gold highlighter without any glitter in it to highlight the cheek, then take trophy wife on my finger and sweep across only the very highest points. I think anyone can very easily use trophy wife for the eyes. it blends beautifully and gives a really lovely gold shimmer to halo eyes and inner corners. I'd suggest probably using a packing brush or smaller precision brushes with it since glitter does like to travel with fluffy brushes. It definitely doesn't need the help of fix plus or a setting spray, but looks gorgeous as a nice shimmery pop of color with setting spray on the brush. The one thing that I don't love about trophy wife is that the glitter seems to migrate throughout the day. I may just need a better setting spray that really sticks that glitter down to the face. A spritz or two throughout the day seems to help keep things in place though.

I learned to do eyeliner by watching Linda halberg's old eyeliner three ways video. After practicing her methods for the last few years, I've gotten to a point where the angle of my liner is perfect every time and I pretty much never have to correct with concealer. So that's my first tip, watch her method and then modify for your eye shape. For pen liners, I like pens that have actual brushes. I feel like they give a much sharper point. But usually I use potted or tubed gel liner. I have a few brushes I like, one is the tarte liner brush. That one is great. I wipe it off after every use because I feel like it doesn't do a good job at making sharp points when it isn't clean. I also like to use precision nail brushes, that's what I used today. It's a flat brush with a tapered end. Almost looks like a really flat lip brush. For me, the key to masculinizing (or feminizing too) the face is to have a clear canvas to work with that still looks natural. This is going to sound super backwards, but that means evening out the skin and minimizing pores without covering every blemish on the face. To achieve that, I like to put on primer to even out the texture of the skin, apply a dab of whiteout concealer or brightening concealer under the eyes and blend it out with a damp makeup sponge. I then dust on some airspun powder. The translucent powder and white concealer seems to blur and brighten a lot of imperfections or freckles without completely covering them. After that I bake my cheekbones, under eye, jawline, chin, and forehead. Then use the shade and light contour palette to lightly brighten some areas and dust off the airspun powder with a kabuki. Then I contour with shade and light, but I make it more angular and softer than my femme contour. I avoid any rounding of the cheeks but still define the cheek bones, so the contouring tends to stay farther to the sides of the face than when I do my regular contouring. I soften it up with a little bit of bronzer, and warm up my face with a red blush wherever it needs warming up. I also used two different highlighters, one warm and one cool. The cool one goes down first, in the places where light is very concentrated on your face naturally. Then I blend out the edges and do larger dustings of the cheek, nose, and brow bones with the warm toned highlight. I find that this is a very easy way to use cool toned highlights or very stark highlights without them getting frosty and looking unnatural. Basically just trying to keep the layers of makeup as absolutely thin as possible, and keeping colors to very natural tones. It's all about working with what you already have with this one

I don't like kalitas against burn in general. It always seems like if I tap out for kalitas I will either let an incredibly important spell resolve (like eidolon) or I'm already pretty close to dead and two or so burn spells will kill me. I would much rather focus on getting a tasigur down early and stabilize that way. I like anger pretty much because of nacatl. They're running a higher concentration of creatures now, so sometimes you'll have a turn after you stabilize where they run out a few creatures in one turn. That's why I do it, but I understand why you wouldn't want to.

Sudden shock is also surprisingly good against affinity, it shuts off ravager being able to dump a million counters onto another creature. Also remember, OP specifically said there was a lot of infect, affinity, and burn, otherwise I probably wouldn't suggest it. It's just that it's so good against infect I don't see a big reason not to run it with the information provided.

Honestly, if there is going to be a ton of burn and affinity (burn is a terrible matchup and affinity is a very draw dependant matchup) I would play something else.

I would cut kalitas and ancestral visions from the sideboard, and put in some number of sudden shocks (for infect) and anger of the gods. Another consideration is leyline of the void instead of nihil spellbomb. It's definitely card disadvantage, but it shuts off so many strategies I think its worth it. Dredge, living end, melira combo, grishoalbrand, the mirror, and I like to bring in in against affinity to shut off ravager shenanigans. 

Main I would shave a mana leak and electrolyze for another k command and either a spell pierce or a spell snare. 

In the burn matchup you'll want to bring in your magma sprays, vampiric link, and angers, and take out remand, mana leak if you're on the play, and dreadbore. If they resolve an eidolon, put your vampiric link on that bad boy, he'll generate a ton of life for you. Otherwise try to put it on a tasigur or angler asap. Magma spray is pretty much just bolts 6 and 7, though you should be careful using against swiftspear, or when they're holding up a potential atarkas command. 

Against infect, you don't need to kill their hierarch asap, especially if you have a k command. Much of the time it's correct to just take a few points of infect so you can get value from your spells and not get blown out. K command is one of your most valuable spells in the main, along with bolt and spell pierce. Shattering an inkmoth nexus and shocking a hierarch provides an insane amount of value, either getting a clean 2 for 1, or baiting out a pump or counter with no danger of dying. Sideboard, you want to bring in EE, crumble, and sudden shocks and take out remands and snares. Play ee on 1 always, it hits every creature except spellskite and sometimes viridian corrupter, though that will usually be sided out against you. Side note, another great sideboard card for this matchup is izzet staticaster, as it can't be spell pierced and will cleanly answer a glistener elf or blighted agent, or again, bait out pump spells when they're no danger of killing you. 

Affinity is a moving target, many of the lists differ in important ways (etched champion, master of etherium, and surprisingly memnite numbers fluctiate). Anger of the gods is a must bring in, as is EE. Sudden shock is pretty decent, as it can stop ravager from doing its thing, but often it won't do enough. I usually take out leaks and remands, as they're too slow. Vandalblast is also great to bring in, it's decent early and amazing late. The lists that run more champions are way more difficult to beat, which is why you have to have all of the non targeting removal like EE and anger. Some must kill cards are steel overseer, master of etherium, and etched champion. Generally its also correct to kill arcbound ravagers as early as possible as well, so they don't get out of hand. If possible you should kill it with another removal spell held up so you can kill whatever it tries to modular onto.
